card.summary: crates.io currently has a 10MB size limit on the `.crate` file.

free_tier.stated: crates.io currently has a 10MB size limit on the `.crate` file.

retention.stated: The version can never be overwritten, and the code cannot be deleted.

egress.terms: Free and unmetered, Cloudflare-fronted, CORS-open. Probe: static.crates.io .crate GET -> 200, Server: cloudflare, Cache-Control: 'public,max-age=31536000,immutable', Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, Accept-Ranges: bytes.

record.tooling: PUT /api/v1/crates/new (binary metadata+body protocol), GET https://static.crates.io/crates/<name>/<name>-<ver>.crate. Clients: cargo publish, cargo-upload style wrappers. No rclone backend.
record.chaining: UNBOUNDED on crates x versions but throttled hard: 5 new crates burst then 1 per 10 minutes; 30 versions burst then 1 per minute. At 10 MB/crate, 10 TiB needs ~1,048,576 crates. At 1 new crate per 10 min that is ~20 years, so crates.io is capacity-unlimited and throughput-useless for bulk. Use it as a low-priority shard, not the primary.

limits.value: 1 new crate every 10 minutes after a burst of 5 new crates
1 new version per minute after a burst of 30 new versions
deletion only if published under 72 hours or single owner and fewer than 1000 downloads per month since publication, and no other crate depends on it

record.limits_note: 10 MB per .crate. Publish rate: burst 5 new crates, then 1 per 10 min; burst 30 new versions, then 1 per minute (documented, leaky-bucket). No delete after 72h unless <1000 downloads/month-per-month AND no dependents AND single owner. Version numbers can never be reused or overwritten.

identity_cost.detail: An email address must be provided and verified on the Account Settings page.

record.reliability_note: Effectively permanent. 'the code cannot be deleted', 'publish is generally permanent'. Excellent durability, terrible write throughput: ~144 crates/day sustained, i.e. ~1.4 GB/day at 10 MB. Never disappears, but you cannot fill it fast.
record.confidence_note: the Cargo publishing page states a 10MB size limit on the .crate file

evidence.proved: 'crates.io currently has a 10MB size limit on the .crate file'; 'There is no limit to the number of versions which can be published'; 'the version can never be overwritten, and the code cannot be deleted'
'allow a burst of 5 new crates published at once by a single user account, with a rate limit of 1 crate every 10 minutes'; 'burst of 30 new versions ... 1 crate per minute'
deletion only if published <72h, or <1000 downloads per month published, and no dependents

evidence.quote: [crates.io](https://crates.io/) currently has a 10MB size limit on the `.crate` file.

evidence.proved: a published version can never be overwritten or deleted
evidence.quote: The version can never be overwritten, and the code cannot be deleted.

evidence.proved: an email address must be provided and verified
evidence.quote: You will also need to provide and verify your email address on the [Account Settings](https://crates.io/settings/profile) page.

evidence.proved: new-crate publishing allows a burst of 5, then 1 crate every 10 minutes
evidence.quote:
For brand new crate publishes, allow a burst of 5 new crates published at once by a single user account, with a
rate limit of 1 crate every 10 minutes allowed after that burst

evidence.proved: new-version publishing allows a burst of 30, then 1 version per minute
evidence.quote:
For new versions of existing crates, allow a burst of 30 new versions published at once by a single user account,
with a rate limit of 1 crate per minute allowed after that burst

evidence.proved: deletion requires publication under 72 hours or a single owner, fewer than 1000 downloads per month since publication, and no dependents
evidence.quote:
Crate owners can delete their crates under certain conditions: the crate has been published for less than 72 hours,
or the crate only has a single owner, the crate has been downloaded less than 1000 times for each month it has been
published, and the crate is not depended upon by any other crate on crates.io.

evidence.proved: rate limits apply to publishing new crates and new versions
evidence.quote: Crates.io has rate limits on publishes of new crates and publishes of new versions of existing crates to mitigate

record.notes: 10 MB per .crate file. No limit on versions per crate ('There is no limit to the number of versions which can be published'), no documented cap on total crates or total bytes per account.
record.binding_note: rate limits apply to publishing new crates and new versions
